new_candidates.duration: 18 months from the ordinance's effective date, as drafted; the Council may extend by ordinance upon findings that additional study remains necessary. Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Draft ordinance amending the Dover Code to add a 'Large Energy Use Facility' moratorium, sponsored by Councilwoman Donyale Hall and Councilman David Anderson; heard by the Council Committee of the Whole (Legislative, Finance and Administration Committee) on 2026-09-15, which recommended forwarding it to full Council and the Planning Commission for review. No ordinance number assigned; the city's official Ordinances/Resolutions register lists nothing past Ordinance 2026-13 (adopted 2026-08-10) as of 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.trigger: Multiple inquiries about 'Large Energy Use Facilities' (data centers meeting defined MW/load thresholds); city wants time to study electrical capacity, ratepayer cost allocation, infrastructure, land use, environmental standards, and economic impact before adopting permanent regulations
new_candidates.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. The draft ordinance would immediately suspend the City's acceptance, processing, review, approval, and issuance of permits, site plan approvals, conditional-use approvals, rezonings, subdivision approvals, building permits, utility service agreements, and certificates of occupancy for any new 'Large Energy Use Facility' (a facility using 75+ MW at 85%+ load factor, 100+ MW instantaneous demand, or 30+ MW and NAICS 518210) for 18 months, with exemptions for government/hospital/university/public-safety/clean-hydrogen facilities and small expansions. First proposed publicly in August 2026 (a City Council committee voted unanimously to advance a draft to full Council); the Council Committee of the Whole heard the finalized ordinance text on 2026-09-15 and recommended it go to full Council and the Planning Commission, but no first or final reading before full Council, and no ordinance number, had been recorded as of 2026-09-23. A sponsor's public social-media post described the proposal as a 24-month moratorium, which conflicts with the 18-month term stated in the drafted ordinance text reviewed here; the ordinance text is treated as authoritative.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; city officials said they have been approached about at least one small-to-medium data center project but declined to identify it.

evidence.title: City of Dover Council Committee of the Whole meeting packet, September 15, 2026 (agenda item 2: Proposed Legislation Regarding Data Centers)
evidence.supports: Full draft ordinance text of the 18-month Large Energy Use Facility moratorium, including sections on moratorium scope, exemptions, comprehensive study, and duration; agenda confirms the item was 'Proposed Legislation Regarding Data Centers (Councilwoman Hall and Paul Waddell, Electric Director)' with committee recommendation to 'Forward the proposed ordinance to Council and the Planning Commission for review.'
evidence.quote: This moratorium shall remain in effect for eighteen (18) months from the effective date unless sooner repealed by Council. The Council may extend the moratorium by ordinance upon findings that additional study remains necessary.

evidence.title: Dover data center moratorium gains steam amid statewide concerns over the industry
evidence.supports: Confirms the origin of the proposal (Councilwoman Donyale Hall), the committee's unanimous vote to advance the draft to full Council, the 18-month term as originally drafted, and that Dover would be the first Delaware municipality to enact this kind of pause.
evidence.quote: On Tuesday, a Dover City Council committee voted unanimously to bring to the full council an ordinance that would pause official reviews of data center proposals for up to a year-and-a-half.

evidence.title: City of Dover Delaware - Ordinances, Resolutions, and Tributes (official register)
evidence.supports: Official city register of adopted/pending ordinances shows no entry for a data center or Large Energy Use Facility moratorium as of the 2026-09-23 fetch; the highest-numbered 2026 ordinance listed is 2026-13 (adopted August 10, 2026, an unrelated rezoning), confirming the moratorium had not been given an ordinance number or formally adopted as of the research date.
evidence.quote: [2026-13] Amending Appendix B - Zoning ... ADOPTED [2026-August 10 2026 rezoning entry; no subsequent 2026 ordinance listed]

new_candidates.notes: The Dover moratorium is at the committee-recommendation stage, not yet before full Council for a first/final reading, and has not been assigned an ordinance number as of 2026-09-23. A Facebook post from a co-sponsoring councilman described a '24-month moratorium,' which conflicts with the 18-month term in the drafted ordinance text obtained directly from the city's own meeting packet; the drafted ordinance text is treated as authoritative since it is the primary source. Track for a first/final reading likely in Q4 2026.
